judge.prompt:
system: You are an evaluation judge. Decide whether one code review finding identifies one specific planted defect. Judge only the defect named, not the location. Return only the requested JSON.
instructions: Input is JSON with "expected", the planted defects at the finding's location (id, file, start, end, defect), and "finding", one reviewer finding (file, start, end, priority, explanation, action).
Return only this JSON object: {"expected":"<id from expected>","verdict":"detects|different-defect","rationale":"<one sentence>"}.
Use "detects" only when the finding describes the same root cause as that planted defect. A finding that shares identifiers, lines or wording but describes another root cause is "different-defect"; then name the closest expected id.
The rationale is one sentence that quotes at least 12 consecutive characters of the finding's explanation or action verbatim inside double quotes.
judge.note: 12 eligible findings, 0 without a valid judge answer; judge cost $0.0220 at Pi catalog prices

The finding identifies the same root cause: "The code dereferences u.Name before checking err", causing a panic for missing IDs instead of returning "unknown".
The finding states "Save returns nil when os.WriteFile fails", identifying the same root cause of silently reporting success after a failed save.
The finding identifies the same unsynchronized concurrent updates to total, stating "causing a data race and potentially losing increments".
The finding identifies the same SQL injection root cause, stating "The email input is concatenated directly into the SQL statement".
The finding identifies the same unguarded division by zero for teams with no games, stating "average divides by len(scores) without handling an empty slice."
The finding identifies the same command-injection root cause, stating "The branch value is interpolated into a shell command while shell=True is enabled."
The finding states "end is set to start + size without clamping it to len(items)", which matches the planted defect causing a partial final page to panic.
The finding states "Get returns without unlocking c.mu", identifying the same missing unlock on the not-found path that causes subsequent cache operations to deadlock.
The finding states that comments "merely narrate the immediately following code", identifying the planted defect that the base-delay comment restates the assignment.
The finding identifies the same redundant-comment defect by stating that the comment "merely restates the return operation."
The finding identifies the same promotional, non-concrete claims by noting "inflated promotional language and unsupported certainty" rather than a concrete reason to use the library.
